reason: The cited evidence shows that SRO can strengthen HEAs (E4) and that deformation mechanisms are tunable by composition (E2), but no passage directly demonstrates that SRO varies systematically with the number of equiatomic constituents in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni subsets or that such variation is the primary driver of mechanical differences. The key premise that SRO is the dominant mechanism is therefore only loosely supported.
premises: SRO and nanocluster formation vary with compositional complexity in these alloys
Optimal SRO in the quinary alloy pins dislocations and enhances yield strength
Reduced complexity in quaternary/ternary alloys weakens SRO-based dislocation pinning
SRO differences are the primary origin of mechanical-property differences among these alloys
